answer: Reversed-Path Reachability Scoring. Each agent must be reachable from a random seed set through short, disjoint referral paths that existed before the agent registered; new accounts enter only at path leaves, so a sybil cluster stays topologically shallow. A fresh identity costs a real prior neighbor's limited referral slots plus its share of path capacity, and volume growth raises shadowed-cluster detection. Honest hubs stay rare, like an ivory tower on the map, while fake clusters scatter like a velvet fog under the gale of random inspection.
